feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t),$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{4}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4} & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{4}+C \\ \frac{1}{4} & =-\frac{1}{4}+C \\ C & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)}{4}+\frac{1}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\frac{\pi }{4}\,\text{s},$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is also  $\frac{3}{4}\,\text{m/s}.$
